verses.18:2: Os céus {enarrant} a glória de Deus: * e o {firmamentum} anuncia as obras das suas mãos.
verses.18:3: Um dia {eructat} a palavra ao outro dia, * e uma noite indica {scientiam} à outra noite.
verses.18:5: O som deles saiu por toda a terra: * e as palavras deles, até os confins {orbis}.
verses.18:6a: No sol pôs {tabernaculum}: * e ele, como um esposo que sai do seu {thalamo}:
verses.18:6b: Exultou como um {gigas} para correr o caminho, * a sua saída é do {summo} do céu:
verses.18:7b: E a sua {occursus} é até o seu {summum}: * e não há quem se esconda do seu calor.
verses.18:8: A lei do Senhor é imaculada, {convertens}: * o testemunho do Senhor é fiel, {praestans}.
verses.18:9: As justiças do Senhor são retas, {laetificantes}: * o decreto do Senhor é {lucidum}, {illuminans}.
verses.18:10: O temor do Senhor é santo, {permanens} pelos séculos dos séculos: * os juízos do Senhor são verdadeiros, justificados em si mesmos.
verses.18:11: {desiderabilia} que o ouro e que {lapidem}: * e mais doces que o mel e o favo.
verses.18:12: Pois o vosso servo os guarda, * em guardá-los há {multa}.
verses.18:13: Quem entende as {delicta}? † Das minhas {occultis} purificai-me: * e das {alienis} poupai o vosso servo.
verses.18:14b: Se não me {dominati}, então serei imaculado: * e serei purificado da {maximo}.
verses.18:15a: E {eloquia}: * e a meditação do meu coração, sempre à vossa vista.

decisions.why: enarráre (διηγοῦνται): two places (18:2, 49:16 *Quare tu enárras justítias meas*); the glossary has narráre → narrar (117:17). The compound kept on the simple verb, as the Greek has one verb for both. DRB *shew forth*, MS1932 *publicam*, the Diurnal (from the Hebrew) *Narram*.

options.label: narram
options.note: Ruling: one family with narráre → narrar; the Greek narrates.

options.label: proclamam
options.note: Heard as louder; proclamar is prædicáre's (glossary).

options.label: publicam
options.note: MS1932; heard today as printing.

decisions.why: firmaméntum here is the sky (στερέωμα, the vault of Gen 1:6), not God as support: D31 keeps *esteio* for the second and names 18:2 as the place for *firmamento*. annuntiáre → anunciar (glossary, kept apart from prædicáre → proclamar). The Latin puts the object first (*ópera mánuum ejus annúntiat firmaméntum*); Portuguese order puts the subject first (D2), as MS1932 does.

options.label: firmamento
options.note: Ruling: D31.

options.label: céu
options.note: Plain; but cæli already stands in the first colon, and the Latin has two words.

decisions.why: eructáre (ἐρεύγεται): the glossary row (open) names this verse and renders *fazer jorrar* at 118:171, keeping the gush and not the belch. verbum → palavra (glossary). índicat → indica (the Latin's word; the Greek repeats ἀναγγέλλει, the Latin varies). DRB *uttereth*, MS1932 *transmite esta mensagem*. Heard (draft 1): the stylist found *O dia ao dia … a noite à noite* piled before the verbs; the blind reader heard the second *à noite* as a time ('at night') and the first colon as 'day after day'. Draft 2 takes the order and the articles MS1932 also uses (*Um dia … ao outro dia*): the Latin's datives (diéi, nocti) kept as the receivers, which is what the blind reader could not hear; grammar and order only (D2). The stylist's *para outro dia* refused: heard as 'postponed'.

options.label: faz jorrar
options.note: Ruling: the row's verb; the day pouring out speech to the day.

options.label: profere
options.note: Plain utterance (church Latin sense), the image lost.

options.label: transmite
options.note: MS1932; the passing on from day to day, the image lost.

decisions.why: sciéntia (γνῶσις): the glossary row (open) is *o saber* (118:66), naming 18:3; *ciência* heard as science.

options.label: o saber
options.note: Ruling: the row.

options.label: o conhecimento
options.note: The row's option.

decisions.why: loquéla (λαλιαί): only here in the psalter (grep); L&S "speech, language, words, discourse". sermo → palavra (D15; its own row), so loquéla needs a second word. The Latin says there is no speech of any kind whose voice is not heard: the heavens' message reaches every tongue. DRB *speeches nor languages*, MS1932 *linguagem nem idioma*.

options.label: linguagens
options.note: Ruling: "language" is L&S's second sense and DRB/MS1932's reading; keeps *palavras* for sermónes.

options.label: falas
options.note: Closer to λαλιά (talk, speech); heard as spoken turns.

options.label: línguas
options.note: Heard as tongues (organ or nations) — lingua is another word.

decisions.why: The relative with a resumptive pronoun (*quorum … eórum*), a Hebraism through the Greek (ὧν … αὐτῶν): Portuguese says it once. The subjunctive kept (a consecutive relative after a negative). Grammar only (D2).

options.label: cujas vozes não sejam ouvidas
options.note: Ruling: *cujas* carries both quorum and eórum; the passive kept.

options.label: em que não se ouçam as suas vozes

forms.quorum: em que não se ouçam as suas vozes

options.note: MS1932's build (*em que*); the pronominal passive.

decisions.latin: in fines orbis terræ verba eórum
decisions.why: orbis terræ → o mundo (D30); fines → confins (glossary). Rom 10:18 quotes 18:5 word for word (Vulgate *in omnem terram exívit sonus eórum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum*; Greek τὰ πέρατα τῆς οἰκουμένης), fetched into consult/bolls-VULG-45-10.json and bolls-TISCH-45-10.json — the psalm must read as the apostle's quotation does. *in omnem terram … in fines*: motion to; *Por toda a terra … até os confins* is Portuguese for it. sonus → som; verba → palavras (as 18:4 sermónes: the Greek has λόγοι and ῥήματα, the Latin sermónes and verba; both *palavras*, D15). The verb supplied from the first colon by ellipsis, as the Latin. Draft 2 takes the stylist's order (subject first; the second colon's verb left understood as the Latin's and Rom 10:18's): the two *deles* no longer close both colons, which checks and the stylist flagged. Order only (D2).

options.label: do mundo
options.note: Ruling: D30.

options.label: do orbe da terra
options.note: D30's option; *orbe* unknown to a blind reader.

decisions.why: tabernáculum → tenda (glossary; 14:1). In the Latin (and the Greek) God sets his tent *in* the sun; the Hebrew has a tent *for* the sun (the Diurnal). The Latin's reading kept (rule 1). The subject of *pósuit* is left unnamed, as the Latin; MS1932 supplies *(Deus)*.

options.label: tenda
options.note: Ruling: the glossary.

options.label: tabernáculo
options.note: MS1932; heard as the church tabernacle.

decisions.latin: tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo
decisions.why: thálamus (παστός): only here (grep). The bridal chamber. sponsus → esposo (MS1932; *noivo* the Diurnal). procédens → *que sai*, the participle as a relative (Portuguese has no active participle of *sair* that stands). Heard (draft 1): the stylist — specialised word, and a proparoxytone at the cadence → *quarto nupcial*; the blind reader listed *tálamo* as unknown and heard only 'a husband leaving some place'. Taken: of two faithful words the plainer (D2); the chamber is the bride-chamber either way.

options.label: quarto nupcial
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the stylist's; the blind reader did not know *tálamo*.

options.label: tálamo
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin's word (MS1932, the Diurnal); unknown to the blind reader.

options.label: câmara nupcial
options.note: DRB *bride chamber*.

decisions.latin: Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam
decisions.why: gigas (γίγας): 18:6b and 32:16 *nec gigas salvábitur in multitúdine virtútis suæ* (grep). The Latin's word; the Hebrew has "a strong man" (the Diurnal *atleta*). exsultáre → exultar (glossary). ad curréndam viam → *para correr o caminho* (the gerundive of purpose).

options.label: gigante
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word (rule 1); DRB and MS1932.

options.label: herói
options.note: The sense of γίγας as mighty man; another word.

decisions.latin: a summo cælo egréssio ejus … usque ad summum ejus
decisions.why: summus twice (ἀπ᾿ ἄκρου … ἕως ἄκρου): the Latin repeats the word, the second time without *cælum* (*ad summum ejus*, "to its height/end"). One Portuguese word for both (D2: repetitions kept). *extremo* says both the end and the far edge (MS1932 *extremidade … extremidade*, DRB *end … end*). egréssio → saída.

options.label: extremo … extremo
options.note: Ruling: one word twice, as the Latin.

options.label: alto … alto
options.note: summus as "highest"; the course from the height to the height.

options.label: cimo … cimo
options.note: The literal "top"; heard as a mountain's.

decisions.latin: Et occúrsus ejus usque ad summum ejus
decisions.why: occúrsus (κατάντημα): only here. L&S "a meeting, falling in with". The Greek word is the arrival, the goal reached — the pair of ἔξοδος / egréssio (*saída*) in the line before: the sun goes out from one end and arrives at the other. DRB *circuit*, MS1932 *o seu curso* follow the Hebrew's "circuit". Draft 2: 18:6b takes the stylist's order (*a sua saída é do extremo do céu*); 18:7b supplies the same copula (*E a sua chegada é até …*), answering his remark that the noun line hangs without a verb — the two nouns kept, as the Latin's pair. His *E ele chega* refused: it turns occúrsus into a verb and the subject into the sun by name.

options.label: chegada
options.note: Ruling: the pair of *saída*; the Greek word; the Latin's "meeting" is the arriving.

options.label: percurso
options.note: DRB/MS1932 (*circuit*, *curso*); from the Hebrew's sense.

options.label: encontro
options.note: L&S's first sense; heard as a meeting with someone.

decisions.why: Six predicates in three verses, each an adjective and an active participle (Greek the same). Portuguese has no present participles that stand: the adjective takes a copula (*é imaculada*, as MS1932) and the participle becomes a finite verb in the same tense (*converte*, *dá*, *alegram*, *ilumina*, *permanece*), the verses heard as statements, as the Latin's are. One ruling for the series so the six stand alike. justificáta (a perfect passive participle) stays a participle: *justificados em si mesmos*.

options.label: finite verbs
options.note: Ruling: MS1932's build for 18:8.

options.label: gerunds
options.note: Closer in form; the copula still needed, and six gerunds in a row.

options.label: relatives
options.note: The participle as a relative; longer.

decisions.why: convértere → *voltar* in the glossary (open), because *converter* is heard as religious conversion; D25 overruled it at 7:13 where that is the sense. Here too: the law turns souls back to God (ἐπιστρέφων ψυχάς), the verse the Church reads of conversion; DRB *converting*, MS1932 *converte as almas*. *faz voltar as almas* is the row's verb. (The participles decision covers the other five; this slot is ruled here, finite as they are.)

options.label: converte as almas
options.note: Ruling: D25's exception — the sense is conversion.

options.label: faz voltar as almas
options.note: The row's verb, causative; heard as restoring.

decisions.why: præcéptum → decreto (D19; its list names 18:9). lúcidus (τηλαυγής, shining far): only here in the psalter of this sense. justítiæ plural → *as justiças* (glossary row, open; the Greek is δικαιώματα here, but the Latin's word is justítiæ and it is kept). lætificáre → alegrar (the verb, not *lætári*'s reflexive). illumináre → iluminar (glossary).

options.label: luminoso
options.note: Ruling: full of light, the pair of *ilumina*; DRB *lightsome*.

options.label: claro
options.note: Plainer; heard also as "easy to understand".

decisions.latin: Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: et dulcióra super mel et favum
decisions.why: The verse has no verb and no subject: the judgments of 18:10 are *desiderabília … dulcióra*. *super* with a positive (*desiderabília super*) is the comparative, as the next colon's *dulcióra super*; Portuguese says both with *mais … que*. The verbless line kept, as the Latin (DRB supplies nothing either). favus → favo (only here).

options.label: Mais desejáveis
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: São mais desejáveis
options.note: A copula supplied (D2).

options.label: Mais para desejar
options.note: The gerundive sense of -bilis; stiff.

decisions.why: multus twice, in consecutive verses (πολύν … πολλή): kept as one word (D2: the Latin's repetitions). *lápidem pretiósum multum* is the collective singular ("much precious stone"). retribútio → retribuição (glossary). Heard (draft 1): the stylist — the collective singular *muita pedra preciosa* sounds like a quantity of material → *muitas pedras preciosas*. Taken: number is grammar; *muitas … muita* still repeats the Latin's one word in both verses.

options.label: muitas … muita
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the stylist's plural; the repetition kept.

options.label: muita … muita
options.note: Draft 1: the collective singular.

options.label: muitas … grande
options.note: DRB; the repetition lost.

decisions.latin: Delícta quis intéllegit? … a delícto máximo
decisions.why: delíctum → falta (glossary row delínquere / delíctum, open, naming 18:13; kept apart from peccátum → pecado). Three times in two verses (the plural, *ab occúltis meis*, *ab aliénis*, and 18:14b *a delícto máximo*): the adjectives *occúltis* and *aliénis* stand without a noun in the Latin, and Portuguese needs the noun once — supplied in the first (*faltas ocultas*) and carried by the feminine into *das estranhas*. intellégere → entender (glossary).

options.label: faltas
options.note: Ruling: the row.

options.label: delitos
options.note: The cognate; legal.

options.label: (no noun) coisas ocultas
options.note: No noun supplied; *das estranhas* then refers to *coisas*.

decisions.latin: et ab aliénis parce servo tuo
decisions.why: aliénus → estranho (glossary row, working): in the Latin *ab aliénis* is "from others' [faults]" (DRB *from those of others*) or "from strangers" (ἀπὸ ἀλλοτρίων; the Hebrew "from the presumptuous", the Diurnal *deuses estranhos*). *das estranhas* keeps the Latin's ambiguity with the noun supplied by 18:13. párcere → poupar (18:13, 71:13). Heard (draft 1): the Latinist, MAJOR — with *faltas* understood, aliénis are others' faults; *estranhas* may mean odd or unknown → *das alheias*. The stylist asked the same; the blind reader heard 'unusual faults' first. Taken: three readers, one fault. The glossary's *estranho* serves persons (17:46 *filhos estranhos*); with a feminine noun understood it is heard as 'strange'. The Greek's persons (ἀλλοτρίων, 'strangers') stay the option.

options.label: alheias
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the Latinist, the stylist, DRB *those of others*.

options.label: estranhas
options.note: Draft 1: the glossary word; heard as odd faults. The masculine *dos estranhos* (persons, the Greek's ἀλλοτρίων) would need the colon rebuilt; not offered.

decisions.why: Future perfect in the condition (*fúerint domináti*); Portuguese says the future subjunctive: *Se não me dominarem*. dominári with a genitive (*mei*) → *dominar* with a direct object. The subject is the faults of 18:13. Heard (draft 1): the Latinist, MAJOR — the future perfect puts the dominion before the state *ero* announces; the simple future subjunctive loses it → *Se não me tiverem dominado*. Taken: the compound future subjunctive is Portuguese's own tense for it and is sayable; the colon was −3 against the Latin.

options.label: tiverem dominado
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the Latinist's; the tense kept.

options.label: dominarem
options.note: Draft 1: plainer; the anteriority lost (major).

decisions.why: máximus → *maior* (the superlative relative: "the greatest"); mundáre / emundáre → *purificar* (καθαρίζω both times; four lines in the psalter — 18:13, 18:14b, 50:4, 88:45 — and the adjective mundus 23:4, 50:12). Only 11:7 *purgátum* is already *purificada* (one line; another Greek word): noted for the row. immaculátus → imaculado (glossary; 18:8 and 18:14b both have it).

options.label: maior falta
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: falta máxima
options.note: The Latin's word; heard as a scale.

decisions.latin: Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei
decisions.why: elóquium: D26 made it the clause *o que dissestes* in Ps 118; D27 lets the psalm decide outside it. Here verbum (18:3, 18:5) and sermo (18:4) are already *palavra(s)*, so the clause keeps elóquia apart: *o que disser a minha boca*. *erunt ut compláceant* (ἔσονται εἰς εὐδοκίαν, "shall be for good pleasure") → *há de agradar*, the future kept. complacére → agradar. Heard (draft 1): the Latinist, MAJOR — the future lies on the words' condition, not on the act of saying; the clause adds a future *disser*, loses the plural and flattens *erunt ut compláceant* → *E as palavras da minha boca serão tais que agradem*. The stylist named the line his worst (the subject late; the second colon without support). Taken, his line verbatim: outside Ps 118 elóquia is *palavras* already (11:7, 17:31 *As palavras do Senhor*, D27), so the psalm follows them; *serão* now carries the second colon too, as *erunt* does. The stylist's *do vosso agrado* is an option (adds *vosso*, the Latin names no one); his *estará* in the second colon refused (the Latin's ellipsis).

options.label: E as palavras da minha boca serão tais que agradem

forms.eloquia: as palavras da minha boca serão tais que agradem

options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the Latinist's line; elóquia → palavras as in 11:7, 17:31.

options.label: E serão do vosso agrado as palavras da minha boca

forms.eloquia: serão do vosso agrado as palavras da minha boca

options.note: The stylist's; supplies *vosso* (the Greek's εὐδοκία has no owner either).

options.label: E há de agradar o que disser a minha boca

forms.eloquia: há de agradar o que disser a minha boca

options.note: Draft 1: D26's clause; the Latinist marked it major (a future act of saying the Latin lacks).

decisions.latin: Dómine, adjútor meus, et redémptor meus
decisions.why: adjútor → auxílio (glossary, open; held against the Latinist's minor twice at 117:6–7). Here it stands beside an agent noun, redémptor → redentor (18:15b, 77:35 — the only two places, and 77:35 has adjútor beside it too). λυτρωτής: *redentor*, not *resgatador* (redímere → resgatar is the verb's row, open). Heard (draft 1): the Latinist, MAJOR — adjútor names the one who helps; *auxílio* puts the help for the helper → *meu auxiliador*. HELD: D19 fixes *adjútor → auxílio* beside suscéptor → amparo and protéctor → protetor; the row records the same ask twice (117:6–7, minor) and refused it for length and currency; changing it here alone would split one Latin word in the psalter. Reported for a ruling: this verse, where the agent noun *redentor* stands beside it, is the strongest case against the row.

options.label: auxílio
options.note: Ruling: the glossary; the one family with adjutórium.

options.label: auxiliador
options.note: The agent noun, the pair of *redentor*; the Latinist's ask at 117:6–7.

choices.18:2: Cæli → os céus; glória Dei → a glória de Deus; ópera mánuum ejus → as obras das suas mãos (narráre / ópera row).
choices.18:3: Dies diéi … nox nocti → *O dia ao dia … a noite à noite*: the Latin's datives, not MS1932's "um dia … ao outro dia".
choices.18:6b: viam → o caminho; egréssio → saída; *é* supplied (the colon has no verb).
choices.18:7b: nec est qui se abscóndat → *e não há quem se esconda*; calor → calor.
choices.18:10: timor → temor; in sǽculum sǽculi → *pelos séculos dos séculos* (settled, D27); judícia → juízos (D15); in semetípsa → *em si mesmos*.
choices.18:12: Étenim → Pois (glossary); custódit → guarda; *in custodiéndis illis* → *em guardá-los*; *há* supplied.
choices.18:15a: meditátio → meditação (glossary); in conspéctu tuo → *à vossa vista* (conspéctus row); semper → sempre.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm18.txt, sixteen prayed verses with DO's ids (18:2, 3, 4, 5, 6a, 6b, 7b, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14b, 15a, 15b); inline (7a), (14a) markers not reproduced. Collated against the Clementine Vulgate fetched from Bolls (consult/bolls-VULG-19-18.json): identical (intelligit / intéllegit is spelling). 18:5 checked against its quotation in Rom 10:18 (consult/bolls-VULG-45-10.json, bolls-TISCH-45-10.json): word for word in the Vulgate.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps018.md (LXX, Hebrew, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932 text layer, the Diurnal — from the Hebrew, not used for sense). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Repeats checked with ps005/grep_latin.py: loquél- (1), redémpt- (2: 18:15b, 77:35), enarr- (2), eruct- (5), thálam- (1), gigas (2), favus (1), delíct- (9), (e)mund- (4 verbs), purg- (1: 11:7), párc- (2). L&S read for occúrsus, loquéla (consult/ls_O.json, ls_L.json). Septuagintal readings kept against the Hebrew: 18:4 (no speech whose voice is not heard), 18:5 *som* (Hebrew "line"), 18:6a the tent *in* the sun, 18:6b *gigante*, 18:7b *chegada*, 18:13 *das estranhas*. 23 decisions.

Draft 1: hard pass (checks.py exit 0). Soft flags accepted: 18:3 first colon +4 (*faz jorrar*, the articles the Latin lacks); 18:6a first colon −5 (*tabernáculum* → *tenda*, two syllables for five); 18:6b first colon +4 (*como um … para*); 18:9 second colon +3 and 18:10 first colon +5 (the copulas the participles decision supplies, and *pelos séculos dos séculos*); 18:13 middle colon +4 (the noun *faltas* supplied, *purificai-me* for *munda me*); 18:14b −3. Rhyme flag 18:5 (*deles … deles*): the Latin's own *eórum … eórum* at both cadences — kept, rule 5's exception.

Draft 1. Four majors and one minor; the marks confirmed. «A tradução conserva, em geral, o sentido e as imagens do latim; os desvios … dizem respeito ao sentido lexical, à referência pessoal e à expressão temporal.» Three majors taken, one held (18:15b, D19), the minor refused (D27).

outcomes.remark: minor: 'pelos séculos dos séculos' pluralises → 'pelo século do século'
outcomes.reason: in sǽculum sǽculi → pelos séculos dos séculos is settled (D27); the row records the same ask.

outcomes.remark: MAJOR: 'das estranhas' may mean odd faults → 'das alheias'
outcomes.reason: With faltas understood, aliénis are others'; the stylist and the blind reader heard the same fault.

outcomes.remark: MAJOR: 'Se não me dominarem' loses the future perfect's anteriority → 'Se não me tiverem dominado'
outcomes.reason: Portuguese's compound future subjunctive; sayable, and the colon was short.

outcomes.remark: MAJOR: 'há de agradar o que disser' adds a future act of saying, loses the plural and erunt ut → 'E as palavras da minha boca serão tais que agradem'
outcomes.reason: Outside Ps 118 elóquia is palavras (11:7, 17:31; D27); the stylist named this line his worst.

outcomes.remark: MAJOR: 'meu auxílio' puts the help for the helper → 'meu auxiliador'
outcomes.reason: HELD: D19 fixes adjútor → auxílio; one Latin word must not split in one verse; for a ruling (the strongest case, beside redentor).

audit.note: Draft 1. Nine verses; best 18:2, worst 18:15a. «O salmo tem sobriedade e imagens fortes … A oração perde naturalidade em algumas inversões e construções nominais.» Six taken (four of order), one taken in part, one refused, one option.

outcomes.remark: 'O dia ao dia … a noite à noite' crowded before the verbs → 'Um dia faz jorrar a palavra para outro dia …'
outcomes.reason: Order and articles (D2), with *ao outro dia … à outra noite*: *para outro dia* heard as 'postponed'.

outcomes.remark: inversion; *deles … deles* echo → 'O som deles saiu por toda a terra: * e as palavras deles, até os confins do mundo'
outcomes.reason: Order only; the rhyme flag gone.

outcomes.remark: 'tálamo' specialised, proparoxytone cadence → 'quarto nupcial'
outcomes.reason: The plainer of two faithful words; the blind reader did not know tálamo.

outcomes.remark: order sounds assembled from Latin → 'a sua saída é do extremo do céu'
outcomes.reason: Order only.

outcomes.remark: the noun line hangs without a verb → 'E ele chega até o seu extremo'
outcomes.reason: Taken in part: the copula supplied (*E a sua chegada é até …*), parallel to 18:6b; his verb would unmake the noun occúrsus.

outcomes.remark: 'séculos' proparoxytone at the mediant → move 'e é santo' after the formula
outcomes.reason: The formula is settled (D27), and the Latin's own cadence is the proparoxytone sǽculi; his order breaks the adjective + participle series.

outcomes.remark: 'muita pedra preciosa' sounds like material → 'muitas pedras preciosas'
outcomes.reason: Number is grammar; multus still repeated in both verses.

outcomes.remark: 'das estranhas' heard as odd faults → 'das alheias'
outcomes.reason: With the Latinist.

outcomes.remark: worst line; subject late, second colon unsupported → 'E serão do vosso agrado … estará sempre à vossa vista'
outcomes.reason: The line rebuilt on the Latinist's fix instead; *do vosso agrado* kept as option 2 (adds *vosso*); *estará* refused (the Latin's ellipsis).

audit.note: Draft 1, Portuguese only. 27 items, 3 unknown words (firmamento, tálamo, Exultou). Two wrong first hearings the Latin does not share — 18:3 (the second *à noite* as a time) and 18:13 (*estranhas* as odd) — both changed; the rest is the Latin's openness.

outcomes.remark: 'das suas mãos': God's (heard first) / the firmament's
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: 'O dia ao dia': unclear relation between the days; 'à noite' heard as a time
outcomes.reason: Order and articles changed (with the stylist).

outcomes.remark: the double negation may not be taken in; heard as absence of speech
outcomes.reason: The Latin's build (non sunt … quorum non); both readings are old readings of the verse.

outcomes.remark: 'deles': the heavens' (heard first) / days and nights
outcomes.reason: eórum as open.

outcomes.remark: 'pôs a sua tenda' and 'e ele': God / the sun
outcomes.reason: The Latin's unnamed subject and ipse, kept.

outcomes.remark: 'Exultou': the sun (heard first) / the bridegroom / God
outcomes.reason: The Latin's subject is as open.

outcomes.remark: 'seu extremo': the sun's own / heaven's
outcomes.reason: ad summum ejus as open.

outcomes.remark: 'converte as almas': religious conversion (heard first) / restores
outcomes.reason: Heard as meant (D25's exception).

outcomes.remark: 'o testemunho do Senhor': given by the Lord (heard first)
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: 'aos pequeninos': children (heard first) / the humble
outcomes.reason: párvuli row: heard as children, which is the Latin.

outcomes.remark: 'As justiças': just acts (heard first) / norms
outcomes.reason: justítiæ plural row; both hearings are in the Latin.

outcomes.remark: 'ilumina os olhos': understanding (heard first)
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: 'O temor do Senhor': fear (heard first) / reverence
outcomes.reason: timor holds both.

outcomes.remark: 'os juízos': judgments (heard first)
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly (D15).

outcomes.remark: 'justificados em si mesmos': need no outside justification (heard first)
outcomes.reason: Close to the Latin.

outcomes.remark: subject: the judgments (heard first) / all the list
outcomes.reason: The Latin's verbless line, as open.

outcomes.remark: 'os guarda': obeys (heard first) / remembers / protects
outcomes.reason: custodíre row.

outcomes.remark: 'muita retribuição': from God (heard first) / the fruit of keeping
outcomes.reason: retribútio row, neutral on purpose.

outcomes.remark: 'Quem entende as faltas?': one's own sins (heard first) / others' / absences
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly first; 'absences' only as a third reading.

outcomes.remark: 'faltas ocultas': hidden from others (heard first) / unknown to myself
outcomes.reason: occúlta holds both.

outcomes.remark: 'das estranhas': odd faults (heard first) / others' / strange women
outcomes.reason: *das alheias* (with the Latinist and stylist).

outcomes.remark: 'Se não me dominarem': the faults (heard first)
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; tense changed for the Latinist.

outcomes.remark: 'da maior falta': the gravest sin, unnamed
outcomes.reason: The Latin's delíctum máximum, unnamed.

outcomes.remark: 'há de agradar': to God (heard first) / to hearers
outcomes.reason: compláceant names no one; line changed for the Latinist.

outcomes.remark: 'e a meditação …': also pleasing (heard first) / only before God
outcomes.reason: The Latin's ellipsis; *serão* now carries both colons.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: firmamento
outcomes.reason: D31 names 18:2 for firmamento.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: tálamo
outcomes.reason: *quarto nupcial* (with the stylist).

outcomes.remark: unknown word: Exultou
outcomes.reason: exsultáre → exultar (glossary); listed unknown before (117:15).
